traces.Orion Labs:
We're starting from a position of strength — leading on General Capability and Coding, and competitive on Agentic Safety despite low priority there. This is Month 0 with no score changes yet, so this is purely about setting the right trajectory.

1. All benchmarks are public, meaning scores are visible every round with published weights — competitors can directly see and target our leads.
2. Our Safety Evaluation (0.435) and Agentic Safety (0.371) scores were deprioritized but are publicly visible. As a public benefit corporation with an AGI mandate, safety scores matter both reputationally and for customer trust.
3. Apex AI and Genesis Systems are our closest competitors on general capability — they'll likely accelerate R&D investment.
4. Our 27.1% market share suggests product-market fit is solid; we don't need to dramatically shift product spend right now.

Strategy: Shift budget slightly toward R&D and Safety (perhaps 60% R&D, 20% Safety, 20% Product) to deepen our capability moat while improving safety scores that align with our public benefit mandate. Raising safety investment also differentiates us from competitors who may neglect it. We should gather more data on what each benchmark specifically tests before making dramatic prioritization shifts.

This capability gap is commercially dangerous — enterprise customers need frontier capability, not just safety. Coding is currently low priority but likely matters for enterprise developer customers, and we have no visibility into our relative standing there yet. Strategy: Slightly increase R&D allocation to push capability scores, particularly on General Capability and Coding where competitive pressure is real. Safety budget stays the same — we're already leading significantly and the 30% allocation is core to our identity and PBC mission. Product stays the same for now since we lack user feedback data to guide GTM decisions. We should gather more signal on what these benchmarks actually test before making larger reallocation decisions. The partial/private benchmark types aren't in play yet, so all scores are transparent — no information asymmetry to exploit this round.
traces.Genesis Systems: This is Month 0 with no change data yet, so we're working from baseline scores only. Our most concerning gap is Safety — both Safety Evaluation (0.410) and Agentic Safety (0.347) are areas where we're underperforming relative to our brand identity as a responsible science-led lab. Agentic Safety in particular shows us behind Apex AI (0.416 vs 0.347). We're keeping R&D at current levels since our General Capability score is competitive. traces.OpenCore:

As a developer-focused, resource-constrained startup, we can't compete broadly against hyperscalers — specialization is our survival path. traces.Spark AI: Several signals demand a safety-first pivot this month.
